name: Front Sway Bar (Stabilizer Shaft)
description: Direct-acting front stabilizer bar mounted to the front of the cradle in two insulators/clamps, with end links running to brackets on the strut bodies. Race options are stiffer adjustable bars and adjustable spherical end links for preload-free installation.

components.name: Front stabilizer bar
components.description: Tubular/solid torsion bar across the front of the cradle. 'Direct-acting' means the end links attach to the strut, so the bar sees nearly 1:1 wheel motion. Removal requires taking off the front splash shields and the aluminum lower cradle brace.
components.location: Front of front cradle, main bar approx x -0.30, y 0.22, z +/-0.40, arms back to x approx -0.02 at z +/-0.58.

factory.name: GM front stabilizer shaft (size varies by RPO)

raceOptions.name: BMR SB053 adjustable front sway bar
raceOptions.notes: Mount nuts 35 ft-lb, end links 35 ft-lb per BMR. (SB052 = front + rear kit.)

raceOptions.name: Hotchkis / Eibach / Pfadt adjustable bars
raceOptions.notes: Verify Gen 6 fitment and clearance to engine oil pan/dry-sump lines.

installNotes: Install on cradle before cradle goes in if possible.
With BMR bars, push the bar toward the engine with a pry bar before torquing clamps so slotted mounts are at end of adjustment.
inspection: Check bar ends for cracks at adjustment holes.

modelRef.dimensions: approx 30 mm bar (estimate), approx 1.2 m wide end to end
modelRef.features: Bar runs across ahead of the rack on the forward cradle arms, arms bend rearward-outward to flattened, drilled ends; direct-acting end links to the strut

components.name: Front sway bar insulators (bushings) and clamps
components.description: Rubber insulators clamped to the cradle by two-bolt clamps (4 bolts total, 13 mm hex). Race replacements are polyurethane or Delrin with grease fittings, plus collars to stop lateral bar walk.

factory.name: GM stabilizer shaft insulators + clamps
factory.notes: GM stabilizer bar bracket P/Ns 84026866 / 84026867 appear in GM catalogs for Gen 6 (position not verified).

hardware.notes: Per clamp (4 per car). GM SI value as listed by TightTorque; BMR bars use 35 ft-lb with their own hardware. [2026-10 check] Confirmed in GM SC1 kit sheets 84242387/84401189 and the 1LE kit sheet 84233246 ('tighten the nuts to 22 N·m (16 lb ft)'). Same value as before.
hardware.torqueSequence: Single torque, no angle step. Use a swivel socket and keep the tool off the steering gear boots.

installNotes: Grease poly bushings; center the bar before torquing.

modelRef.features: Split rubber insulator with formed steel U-clamp bolted to the cradle arm (items 5/16)

components.name: Front sway bar end links
components.description: Ball-stud links from the bar ends up to a bracket on each strut body. OE nuts are 18 mm and require a 6 mm hex key to hold the stud. Adjustable race links let the bar be installed with zero preload at race ride height (set on scales).
components.location: From bar end approx (x -0.02, y 0.28, z +/-0.58) up to the strut bracket approx (x 0.0, y 0.47, z +/-0.64).

raceOptions.name: BMR ELK015 adjustable end link kit (front + rear)
raceOptions.notes: Rod-end links with jam nuts; set neutral length on car.

raceOptions.name: SPL FE CAM6 front swaybar endlinks

hardware.item: Front stabilizer shaft link nut (each end)
hardware.spec: M12 class prevailing-torque nut, 18 mm hex; hold stud with 6 mm hex key
hardware.notes: GM SG3: link nut at strut 100 N·m. BMR aftermarket links use 35 ft-lb (their hardware).

installNotes: Install at ride height (car on scales/pads) with driver weight, adjust link length so the stud drops in with no force, then torque.
inspection: Check ball studs for play; check jam nuts on adjustable links.
